Business API map

How the business runs through the Bunkai TMS API. Built from the app repo at origin/staging (de0ee80): the generated contract public/openapi.json (Bunkai TMS API 0.1.0) and the route handlers behind it. This is a narrative, not an endpoint catalog: the contract is the catalog.

Overview

The API lets a QA team do in code everything it does in the browser: author anchored test cases, chain them into Tests, execute Runs and record every step's result, file and triage Bugs, plan and report. A CI pipeline or an AI agent signs in once, keeps a Personal Access Token, and drives the same loop a person drives in the UI, under the same permissions.

It also carries the moments where money and data move: a paid upgrade through Stripe Checkout, a full workspace export, and a workspace deletion with a 30-day grace period. Those paths accept a browser session only, or are reached by Stripe and the scheduler rather than by people.

One rule shapes everything: the database, not the API, is the last line of defence. Every request becomes a database call that runs either as the caller (row-level security applies) or through a business function that re-checks the caller's membership itself. A route that forgets a check still cannot read another workspace.

Permission and auth model

Every route declares its tier in withApiHandler; anything not marked public requires an identity. The contract declares three security schemes: cookieAuth, bearerAuth and cronAuth.

How a PAT call becomes a database call

  1. resolveIdentity reads Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret> first, the session cookie otherwise.
  2. The prefix finds the token row; the secret's SHA-256 must match; revoked or expired tokens fail. Every failure is the same 401, so a caller cannot probe tokens.
  3. The route checks the capability it needs against the token's scopes (403 forbidden when missing).
  4. The API mints a 60-second HS256 JWT for the token's user, signed with SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, and queries Postgres with it: RLS applies to a PAT exactly as to a browser. Without that secret every Bearer call fails with 500.
  5. last_used_at is updated without delaying the response.

Conventions every client meets

  • Error envelope: every error carries a code, an HTTP status and the request id; validation errors are 422; business codes such as project_limit_reached (422), checkout_in_progress (409), no_executable_steps (422) and payment_processor_unavailable (503) are named in lib/api/error-envelope.ts.
  • Request id: an inbound x-request-id is reused, otherwise generated; quote it in bug reports.
  • Idempotency: Idempotency-Key (8 to 128 characters, [a-zA-Z0-9_-]) is REQUIRED on four writes: POST /api/v1/runs, POST /api/v1/tests, POST /api/v1/test-plans/{id}/tests and POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout; missing → 400 idempotency_key_required. Marking, finishing and aborting do not use it: the Run row lock and the "first terminal call wins" rule make a retry safe there. The same key and body replay the first answer for 24 hours; a different body answers 409.
  • Non-disclosure: an object in another workspace answers 404, never 403, so the API never confirms it exists.

Journey: execute a Run

The core value of the product: a person, an agent or CI executes a Test and leaves immutable evidence.

  1. POST /api/v1/runs with test_id, environment_id and, for a PAT, executor_mode (run:execute, Idempotency-Key required). The handler resolves the workspace for the idempotency namespace, then bunkai_create_run freezes the snapshot. Why: a retried start must not create two Runs, and later ATC edits must not change this one.
  2. GET /api/v1/runs/{id} returns the Run with its ATCs and steps; the browser also subscribes to Supabase Realtime for live marks.
  3. POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark per step (passed, failed, blocked; note optional). The function locks the Run row so marks never race a finish or abort.
  4. POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/finish with a verdict, or POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/abort with a reason. The first terminal call wins; the API passes via = cookie or bearer so the notification trigger knows whether the ender was a person at the screen.
  5. GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/compare compares with the previous finished Run of the same Test and environment.

Failure answers: 422 environment_invalid or no_executable_steps; 409 when the Run is already closed; 400 without an Idempotency-Key; 404 for a Run in another workspace.

Entities: business-data-context entity-run-snapshot, flow-run-execution, state-run. Features: business-e2e-context feature-runs (FEAT-011, FEAT-012).

Journey: author anchored test cases

Traceability by construction: no test case exists without the business criterion it proves.

  1. POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/modules, POST /api/v1/modules/{id}/user-stories, POST /api/v1/user-stories/{id}/acceptance-criteria build the structure (atc:write).
  2. POST /api/v1/atcs with steps, assertions and at least one criterion id. bunkai_create_atc checks that every criterion belongs to the ATC's story (422 ac_outside_user_story) and the module to the project subtree, then writes everything and the audit row in one transaction.
  3. PATCH /api/v1/atcs/{id} replaces steps and assertions; the response lists the Tests the edit affects.
  4. POST /api/v1/atcs/{id}/duplicate, GET /api/v1/atcs/search, GET /api/v1/atcs/{id}/usage, GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/atcs/export (CSV).

Entities: entity-atc, flow-authoring. Features: feature-authoring (FEAT-005 to FEAT-008).

Journey: file and triage a Bug

Turns a failed step into owned work, keeping the evidence attached.

  1. POST /api/v1/bugs with severity, module and, when it comes from a Run, the run, step and ATC ids (atc:write). A trigger rejects provenance that does not belong together.
  2. GET /api/v1/bugs/{id} returns the Bug with its origin (the Run and the failed step position) or none for a standalone Bug.
  3. POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/assign and POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/status (forward one stage). Both call their function through the caller's RLS client, never the service role, so auth.uid() is the caller: a browser session directly, a PAT through its short-lived user JWT.
  4. Each change writes an activity row; a trigger turns it into notifications.

Entities: entity-bug, flow-bug-filing, state-bug. Features: feature-bugs (FEAT-013, FEAT-014).

Journey: upgrade to the paid plan

The only revenue path.

  1. GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing: plan, seats, projects, oldest-run age (admin or owner; 404 otherwise).
  2. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout (Idempotency-Key required, admin or owner): the API inserts the open checkout row first (409 checkout_in_progress if one is open), then creates the Stripe Checkout Session with that row's id as client_reference_id, and returns Stripe's URL. Why first: the row can always be found again, even if the app crashes after Stripe answers.
  3. The browser pays on Stripe's hosted page and returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1.
  4. Stripe calls POST /api/v1/billing/webhook. The route verifies the signature (400 without it), handles four checkout events and answers 200 ignored for every other type. bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event sets the plan to cloud only when the payment is paid and records the event id so a redelivery is a no-op.
  5. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout/cancel releases an open checkout.

Failure answers: 422 plan_not_upgradable, 422 seat_quantity_invalid, 503 payment_processor_unavailable when Stripe cannot be reached.

Entities: flow-billing-upgrade, state-billing-checkout. Features: feature-administration (FEAT-025, FEAT-026).

Journey: export and delete a workspace

Where all of a team's data leaves the product or ends. Owner only, browser session only: a PAT gets 403 on every step.

  1. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/data-export enqueues the export; a Vercel after() worker builds the archive in private Storage. GET …/data-export polls; GET …/data-export/download streams it after re-checking owner, ready and not expired (no signed URL is ever handed out).
  2. DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id} requests deletion: access ends for everyone, members are emailed, purge in 30 days.
  3. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/restore during the grace period undoes it.

Entities: flow-workspace-export, flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace. Features: FEAT-027, FEAT-028.

Journey: import stories from Jira

Brings the backlog in so ATCs can anchor to real criteria.

  1. POST /api/v1/imports (atc:write) enqueues a job and answers at once; 409 import_in_progress if the project already has one running.
  2. The job runs in the Vercel after() slot with the service-role client, paging Jira's search with the deployment's Jira credentials and retrying on 429.
  3. GET /api/v1/imports/{id} polls status, counts and per-issue errors.

Entities: flow-jira-import, state-async-jobs. Features: FEAT-007.

Architecture behind the API

One Next.js application on Vercel serves both the UI and /api/v1; each route handler is a serverless function. There is no separate backend service and no queue. Background work runs in Vercel's after() slot (Jira import, workspace export), on Vercel Cron (daily digest) and on pg_cron inside Postgres (run inactivity sweep, workspace purge).

Handlers reach the database in two ways:

  • As the caller (principal.db): an RLS-scoped client, for a cookie or a PAT alike.
  • Through the service-role client plus a bunkai_* function that takes the actor explicitly and re-checks membership and role itself. About half the route files use it (Runs, Bugs, ATCs, reports, billing, invites). Since those calls bypass RLS, the function's own checks are the isolation; two isolation defects of this kind already shipped and were fixed (migrations 0047 and 0089).

Cross-references

  • Full contract: public/openapi.json in the app repo (generated from each route.openapi.ts by bun run openapi:gen), served at /api/openapi and browsable at /api/docs on each environment (URLs in .agents/project.yaml).
  • TypeScript types: api/schemas/ in this repo, refreshed by bun run api:sync. Today it holds only auth.types.ts and an example: the sync has not been run against the current contract.
  • Entities: bun run context:map business-data-context (each journey above names its sections).
  • Features and journeys: bun run context:map business-e2e-context; its api-inventory section lists the domains.
  • Auth flow details and NFRs: bun run context:map infra-context.

Coherence checks done for this map: every journey touches entities present in the data map; every journey maps to e2e features; every integration in the e2e map's integrations section appears here. Tracker settings (FEAT-029) reach the API but no outbound Jira call exists yet for them.

Discovery gaps

  • The Stripe webhook is not in the contract: POST /api/v1/billing/webhook exists as a route but has no route.openapi.ts entry in public/openapi.json.
  • api/schemas/ is stale: generated types cover auth only; bun run api:sync has not been run against the 86-path contract.
  • Infra map drift: infra-context was generated from a local clone 537 commits behind staging; its auth-flow section may miss later changes (for example cronAuth and the Stripe secrets).
  • Rate limiting: no application rate limiter was found beyond relaying Supabase's OTP 429.
  • Journey cap: 6 journeys are traced. Test Plans, notifications, saved views, search and the reports are API-backed too and left to the e2e map's feature catalog.
  • No live calls: this map was built from source and the contract; no request was sent to staging.
